study.question: Which embedding-input role carries the predictive benefit of differentiable normalization-support rows: the repeated target query, the compressed historical values/action, or their interaction? Observed limitation: g0-r0023-moment_both reproduced g0-r0022-support_rotated_attached at click AUC0.666753547526167, while mean-only0.6650149110872101 and variance-only0.6654753133736193 underperformed even neither0.6661241491820656. Their simultaneous change to multiple upstream sources leaves gradient ownership unresolved. Candidate diagnostics were not requested in those receipts, so the partial-kernel implementation remains an alternative explanation.
study.hypothesis: With native mean/variance derivatives kept coupled, the additional support population may improve history representation learning while its repeated target-query feedback is unnecessary or conflicting. Stopping only the support target-query input path while retaining support history-value/action learning should preserve or improve click AUC versus the both-attached incumbent, and outperform stopping the history-value path. This is a provisional role-specific optimization hypothesis, not evidence of a new information source or an established mechanism. Earlier compressed task queries (g0-r0006-compressed_task/shared) failed to beat the source; target-match residuals and coarse curvature helped in g0-r0009-match_detail_task and g0-r0014-curvature_task; joint features (g0-r0016-joint_ordered), local block energy (g0-r0018-block_energy_local), aligned feedback (g0-r0020-feedback_aligned) and partial moment derivatives did not beat their relevant controls. These trajectories argue for attribution before another information channel.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary v4 text lines317..335 describes Dice with batch mean/variance and moving test statistics; lines75..88 describe target-dependent local activation. Inherit those operators and the locally adapted multifeedback compressor, while changing only gradient ownership of extra rows excluded from prediction readout. No original-DIN reproduction or priority claim.

Pinned commit90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d implements Dice as sigmoid(BatchNorm1d affine=False, eps1e-9, momentum0.01), then alpha-gated linear channels. Leave this complete native module unchanged; gate only the target/history operands before support interactions. Avoid the corrective mean/variance surrogate used in mixed r0023 cells.

Exact available candidate source, hash63ce570394d1645fffa5950198fbdd6c9a86ef9ac0376c5fc121e12690ab69f6, is the closest model. Its support_gradient blocked control detaches preactivations before every Dice, jointly blocking several scorer and embedding paths. New factorial stops only selected support input operands; scorer parameters and all downstream normalization paths remain trainable.

Original LONGER source is link-only (paper:longer); original-method novelty and broader coverage remain unverified.

study.proposed_difference: Add two boolean architectural routing switches: support_query_gradient and support_value_gradient. Only during training, in the primary 70-row interaction construction, apply torch.where over stratum index modulo7 to replace rows3..6 of the expanded target query and/or compressed value tensor with its detach. Rows0..2 keep full gradients. Build query, keys, query-minus-keys, query-times-keys and historical action from these operands after gating, covering every query/value occurrence. Leave _interactions for auxiliary use and _primary_activation native attached. Both-attached and evaluation call the original interaction builder exactly. No learned modules, loss hook, state, RNG, source information, compression/readout assignments or host settings are added. Target and history roles share embedding tables; claims are branch-local. Neither-input is deliberately not the pre-Dice-detached r0022/r0023 control.
predictions: At a fixed state in train and eval, all four cells have the same four prediction tensors and persistent buffers within host precision tolerances; both-attached must reproduce g0-r0022-support_rotated_attached/g0-r0023-moment_both before interpreting differences.

Using isolated leaf query and compressed-value operands for support rows, blocked-role interaction derivatives are zero, attached-role derivatives match native interaction derivatives, and row0..2 interaction Jacobians are unchanged. Shared scorer gradients can remain nonzero even with both support inputs stopped. Full-network table gradients and main-row paths can change through batch coupling.

Primary directional prediction: support_history_only AUC is at least both-attached and exceeds support_query_only; stopping support values at either fixed query setting tends to hurt. Practical improvement requires exceeding incumbent and both frozen source bests at measured cost, rather than matching them.

Estimate role contrasts with Q,V in {0,1}: A01-A11 (stop query with history attached), A10-A11 (stop values with query attached), A00-A10, A00-A01; interaction A11-A10-A01+A00. Q=target-query gradient and V=historical-value/action gradient. Treat single-seed contrasts as preliminary.

Report actual wall/GPU time, peak memory and inference throughput/latency; no efficiency claim from parameter equality.

Use only authorized full validation: report click AUC/Logloss, each auxiliary task AUC/Logloss, auxiliary mean separately, and existing predeclared empty/1..16/17..64/>64 history bins with samples, positives and negatives. These bins are inherited; slice differences are exploratory and not an independent selection score. Paired seeds and paired user-cluster bootstrap are deferred unless a later host interface supplies them within budget; none are fabricated from aggregate receipts.
falsifiers: Failure of fixed-state prediction/buffer parity, branch-specific derivative isolation, finite gradients or bridge reproduction invalidates mechanistic interpretation; do not interpret numerical failure as scientific counterevidence.

If support_history_only is below both-attached, useful removal of repeated target-query feedback is unsupported in this implementation. If stopping historical values does not harm or improves at both fixed query settings, the predicted historical-input benefit is unsupported.

If neither-input matches both-attached while historical pre-Dice blocking remains worse, embedding feedback is not necessary for the observed advantage and scorer/internal normalization paths become a more plausible next question. This cross-round contrast is provisional until matched repetition.

If both single-input cells lose and both-attached wins, role complementarity remains plausible but the selective routing candidate fails. One seed establishes neither repeated support nor statistical significance.
Any apparent gain explained by changed capacity, recipe, sample visibility, bridge mismatch or unacceptable measured runtime is not support for the intended isolated mechanism.
alternative_explanations: Coupled mean/variance gradients are coherent jointly, while the previous custom partial cancellation may amplify BF16/epsilon differences. Native Dice in this study removes that custom mixed-kernel factor but does not retrospectively validate its Jacobians.
The benefit may primarily train shared scorer parameters and Dice alpha rather than embeddings; neither-input retains these paths, unlike repeated pre-Dice detach.

Batch composition, padding and empty support rows affect Dice; their forward population is deliberately unchanged and may account for apparent advantages independently of semantic target/history alignment.

Detaching one role changes sparse Adagrad accumulators and optimization conditioning of a shared embedding table; it cannot prove semantic history learning or absence of target contributions through the retained readout/residual paths.

Single-seed optimization, multiple validation comparisons, auxiliary-task competition and validation slices can explain small differences. All four task metrics are required and stronger click performance need not improve auxiliary AUC.
